note: For inputs larger than 64 bytes, the final 64 raw input bytes are copied directly into the UTF-32 text array that will be shaped.
The copied UTF-32 values are appended to a HarfBuzz buffer as Unicode codepoints; the candidate tail includes Arabic codepoints that select Arabic shaping and combining mark processing.
The first strong non-common codepoint from the fuzzer-controlled UTF-32 text sets the buffer script to Arabic.
An Arabic horizontal buffer is routed to the Arabic complex shaper, whose shaper descriptor installs reorder_marks_arabic.
The selected Arabic shape plan and the fuzzer-populated buffer enter normalization before glyph substitution.
A short run of non-zero combining-class Arabic marks from the input is sorted in place during the second normalization round.
Because the Arabic shaper is active, the sorted combining-mark run is passed to reorder_marks_arabic.
The fuzzer-controlled Arabic modifier combining marks make j advance past one or more MCM entries.
The guard only skips when no MCM range is found; when i differs from j, the function proceeds to cluster merging during an in-place reorder pass.
The Arabic reordering code calls an out-buffer cluster helper even though this normalization pass is operating on buffer->info in place.

merge_out_clusters compares cluster data from out_info while extending the start of the range; in this call path that storage can be stale or uninitialized, which is the MSan use-of-uninitialized-value.
The loop continues to consume out_info cluster fields for the fuzzer-selected mark range, propagating the uninitialized value into cluster computation.
